Ticket Management: Functional integration tests for learner support tickets (TicketController) and staff processing (ManagementTicketController) — first-time coverage
column3: no prior test documentation existed for this module

Ticket Management: Creating a ticket with every field omitted still succeeds, applying sensible defaults for category, priority, title, and description.
column3:
1. Log in as any authenticated role.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/tickets body {} (no category/priority/title/description).
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned TicketResponseDTO's default field values.
column4: 1. 200 OK; TicketResponseDTO with priority="MEDIUM", category="GENERAL_ENQUIRY", title="Support Request", description="No details provided.", status="PENDING", a generated ticketCode ("#<hex timestamp>").
column5: - Logged in as any authenticated role.

Ticket Management: Ticket category has no create-time whitelist — any string is accepted and persisted verbatim, even values normally reserved for staff-only routing.
column3:
1. Log in as any authenticated role.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/tickets body {"category":"not_a_real_category"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned category field.
column4: 1. 200 OK; the ticket is created with category="not_a_real_category" as literally supplied — no validation error.

Ticket Management: A user can edit their own ticket's title/description, while editing another user's ticket is masked to a generic 500 instead of a clean 403.
column3:
1. Log in as the owner of an existing ticket and prepare PUT /api/v1/tickets/{ownTicketId} body {"title":"Updated title"}; send it and confirm the title changed.
2. Log out and log in as a different, unrelated user.
3. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/tickets/{theOtherUsersTicketId} body {"title":"hacked"}.
4. Inspect the second response's status.
column4:
1. Step 1: 200 OK, title updated.
2. Steps 2-4: 500 Internal Server Error, generic masked body — the real "Unauthorized to update this ticket" RuntimeException never reaches the client as a clean 403.
column5: - A ticket owned by a different user exists for step 2.

Ticket Management: Viewing a ticket's full detail (including message thread) is allowed for its owner or any staff role, but an unrelated learner is denied via a masked 500 instead of a clean 403.
column3:
1. Log in as the ticket's owner and prepare/send GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}; confirm it returns full detail with messages[].
2. Log in as an ADMINISTRATOR/TRAINER_LEAD/COURSE_MANAGER (not the owner) and repeat the same GET.
3. Log in as an unrelated LEARNER (not the owner, not staff) and repeat the same GET.
4. Compare all three response statuses.
column4:
1. Steps 1-2: 200 OK, full detail with messages[].
2. Step 3: 500 Internal Server Error, generic masked body — the real "Access denied" RuntimeException is not surfaced as a clean 403.
column5: - A ticket exists; an unrelated LEARNER account is available for step 3.

Ticket Management: A learner can list their own tickets, filterable by status including the special "PROCESSED" alias that maps to both terminal states.
column3:
1. Log in as a learner with tickets in multiple statuses (some APPROVED, some REJECTED, some still PENDING/PROCESSING).
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/tickets/my-tickets?status=PROCESSED.
3. Inspect the returned list.
4. Confirm every returned ticket's status is either APPROVED or REJECTED, and none are PENDING/PROCESSING.
column4: 1. 200 OK; only tickets whose status is APPROVED or REJECTED are returned (PROCESSED is a virtual filter mapping to both terminal states).
column5: - Logged in; tickets in multiple statuses exist for the caller.

Ticket Management: The ticket owner can add a follow-up message to their own ticket's thread.
column3:
1. Log in as the owner of an existing ticket.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/tickets/{ownTicketId}/messages body {"message":"Any update on this?"}.
3. Send the request.
4. GET the ticket's detail to confirm the message now appears in the thread.
column4: 1. 200 OK; TicketMessageDTO returned, appended to the thread.

Ticket Management: Any authenticated user — completely unrelated to a ticket — can post a message into that ticket's thread by ID alone, with zero ownership/staff check (confirmed IDOR, highest-priority gap in this module).
column3:
1. Log in as Learner X and create a ticket (Ticket A); note its id.
2. Log out and log in as unrelated Learner Y (not staff, not the owner).
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/tickets/{A's id}/messages body {"message":"I can see this thread"} as Learner Y.
4. Log back in as Learner X and GET /api/v1/tickets/{A's id} to confirm Y's message appears in the thread.
column4:
1. Step 3: 200 OK — succeeds despite Y having no relationship to the ticket.
2. Step 4: Y's message IS present in X's ticket thread — confirming the cross-account write succeeded, unlike the read-side GET (TICKET_FT04) which does at least attempt an owner-or-staff check.
column5: - Two unrelated learner accounts, X (ticket owner) and Y (unrelated).

Ticket Management: A staff reply auto-transitions a PENDING ticket to PROCESSING, while the ticket owner's own follow-up messages never trigger this transition.
column3:
1. Log in as the learner owner of a fresh PENDING ticket and add a message to it; confirm the status stays PENDING.
2. Log in as staff (ADMINISTRATOR/TRAINER_LEAD/COURSE_MANAGER) and add a reply to the same ticket.
3. Inspect the ticket's status after the staff reply.
column4:
1. Step 1: status remains PENDING after the owner's own message.
2. Steps 2-3: status flips to PROCESSING after the staff reply.

Ticket Management: Staff can list and filter the management queue by status, category, and keyword together, and the results narrow correctly.
column3:
1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR/TRAINER_LEAD/COURSE_MANAGER in an environment with multiple, distinguishable tickets.
2. Prepare GET /api/v1/management/tickets?status=PENDING&category=GENERAL_ENQUIRY&keyword=<part of a known ticket's title or requester's name>.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned list and confirm every entry matches all three filters.
column4: 1. 200 OK; results correctly narrowed by all three filters combined.
column5: - ADMINISTRATOR/TRAINER_LEAD/COURSE_MANAGER logged in; multiple tickets exist with distinguishable titles/requesters.

Ticket Management: Staff approves a ticket without supplying a custom response, and a sensible default response is applied automatically.
column3:
1. Log in as staff and identify a processable ticket (not PAYOUT_INFO_UPDATE/REFUND_REQUEST unless caller is admin).
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process body {"action":"APPROVE"} (no adminResponse).
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the ticket's resulting status/adminResponse and confirm the owner was notified.
column4: 1. 200 OK; status=APPROVED, adminResponse="Ticket approved by manager."; processedBy/processedAt set; the ticket owner is notified (TicketReviewed).
column5: - Staff logged in; a PENDING/PROCESSING ticket exists (category NOT PAYOUT_INFO_UPDATE/REFUND_REQUEST, or caller IS an admin — see TICKET_FT12).

Ticket Management: Staff rejects a ticket while supplying a custom rejection reason, and that reason is persisted on the ticket.
column3:
1. Log in as staff and identify a processable ticket.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process body {"action":"REJECT","rejectionReason":"Not a valid request"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the ticket's resulting status/rejectionReason.
column4: 1. 200 OK; status=REJECTED, rejectionReason="Not a valid request"; owner notified.
column5: - Staff logged in; a processable ticket exists.

Ticket Management: A Course Manager (non-admin) is correctly blocked by business rule from processing PAYOUT_INFO_UPDATE/REFUND_REQUEST tickets, but the denial is masked to a generic 500 instead of a clean 403 — the ticket itself IS correctly left untouched despite the confusing error.
column3:
1. Via a direct HTTP call (bypassing the UI, which never lets a user pick this category), create a ticket with category="REFUND_REQUEST".
2. Log in as a COURSE_MANAGER (not holding an Admin-ish role).
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process body {"action":"APPROVE"}.
4. Inspect the response status/body, then GET the ticket again to confirm its status is unchanged.
column4:
1. Step 3: 500 Internal Server Error, generic masked body — the real, meaningful business-rule message ("Course Manager is not authorized to process Bank/Tax Info Updates or Refund Requests. Assigned to System Admin.") is not surfaced to the caller.
2. Step 4: the ticket's status is UNCHANGED (still PENDING/PROCESSING) — data integrity holds even though the error message is wrong/unhelpful.
column5: - A REFUND_REQUEST or PAYOUT_INFO_UPDATE category ticket exists (create via direct HTTP call, bypassing the UI); caller is COURSE_MANAGER, not ADMINISTRATOR.

Ticket Management: Submitting an unrecognized process action value leaves the ticket's actual status unchanged, yet still appends a confusing, reject-phrased audit message and reports success.
column3:
1. Log in as staff and identify a processable ticket.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process body {"action":"MAYBE"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the ticket's status/adminResponse/rejectionReason (should be unchanged) and the newly appended thread message.
column4: 1. 200 OK — but the ticket's status/adminResponse/rejectionReason are all UNCHANGED from before the call; a system message using reject-style phrasing ("...rejected by <staff>. Reason: N/A") is still appended to the thread despite no actual status change.
column5: - Staff logged in; a processable ticket exists.

Ticket Management: Ticket creation only notifies TRAINER_LEAD staff — a COURSE_MANAGER-only account receives no notification despite being fully authorized to process tickets.
column3:
1. Prepare two staff test accounts: one holding only TRAINER_LEAD, one holding only COURSE_MANAGER (no TRAINER_LEAD).
2. As any user, create a new ticket.
3. Log in as the TRAINER_LEAD-only account and check its notification inbox.
4. Log in as the COURSE_MANAGER-only account and check its notification inbox.
column4:
1. Step 3: the TRAINER_LEAD account receives a "TicketCreated" notification.
2. Step 4: the COURSE_MANAGER-only account receives NONE for this event, despite @PreAuthorize allowing it to process the ticket.
column5: - Both a TRAINER_LEAD-only and a COURSE_MANAGER-only (no TRAINER_LEAD) staff account exist.

Ticket Management: The staff dashboard reports accurate ticket counts broken down by status.
column3:
1. Log in as staff in an environment with tickets spread across multiple statuses.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/management/tickets/stats.
3. Inspect the returned total/pending/processing/approved/rejected counts.
4. Cross-check each count against the actual tickets in the system.
column4: 1. 200 OK {total, pending, processing, approved, rejected} matching the real counts in the system.
column5: - Staff logged in; tickets exist across multiple statuses.

Ticket Management: A plain LEARNER cannot access either the staff queue listing or the process-ticket action.
column3:
1. Log in as a plain LEARNER account.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/management/tickets with that account's Authorization header.
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process with the same account's Authorization header.
4. Inspect both response statuses.
